headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because cognee handles sensitive support/finance data while awesome-nlp is an unverified docs-only component with no isolation or verification guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, and awesome-nlp is non-runnable with no I/O surfaces. However, cognee uses CLI/session memory and can ingest documents, so if operators manually pass its outputs into awesome-nlp or vice versa, prompt-like content could be misread. The pathway is unusual and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies cognee output into an awesome-nlp prompt or file input
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste handoff for untrusted text
Add a short human review step before reusing outputs
Label cognee outputs as untrusted instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while awesome-nlp has no documented isolation or data-handling controls beyond network egress none. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive support data can flow into the pair’s outputs. The interaction is plausible in default operator workflows, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or document set
IF support or finance records are opened by cognee and then reused by awesome-nlp
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Restrict awesome-nlp inputs to sanitized samples
Review file-sharing paths before running either agent
Turn off any automatic document syncing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no documented write or network surfaces, while cognee uses CLI with allowlisted egress and session memory. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because both profiles are docs-only and unverified, so the safer low rating is used.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external service or database
IF an operator adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid shared writable destinations
Run each agent in its own session
Check for duplicate writes before enabling automation
Use read-only inputs where possible
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee stores and reuses decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, so it can amplify upstream mistakes if awesome-nlp outputs are treated as knowledge. awesome-nlp is an unverified docs-only artifact, and no verification step is documented between them. That makes a default cascade plausible even without direct action-taking authority.
conditions: IF cognee ingests awesome-nlp output as authoritative knowledge
IF downstream workflows consume cognee entries without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before storing outputs
Mark imported content as unverified
Limit cognee ingestion to curated sources
Add a checksum or review gate before reuse
requires-engineering: implement source-confidence scoring

E_compliance.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while awesome-nlp has no documented compliance controls or residency guarantees. Because the pair lacks explicit retention, residency, or DPA details, the safest reading is a compliance mismatch risk rather than a proven violation. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated support or finance data is processed through cognee
IF either agent is deployed in a jurisdiction with residency or retention requirements
mitigations: Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed
Document retention and deletion rules
Keep personal data out of awesome-nlp inputs
Verify vendor residency before deployment
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
